I stopped by the pharmacy to pick up a routine prescription, one I'd refilled dozens of times before, the kind of errand I barely even think about anymore.
I expected the whole thing to take maybe five minutes at most.
The pharmacist called a name that sounded close enough to mine and handed me a white paper bag.
I said thanks, tossed it in my bag, and headed straight home without really thinking twice.
It wasn't until later that evening, opening the bag to actually take the medication, that I noticed the name on the label wasn't quite mine.
It was just similar enough that I'd completely missed it earlier.
I actually read it twice before it registered, one letter off from my own last name.
It was close enough that my brain had just automatically filled in the rest without really questioning it.
Turns out, there was apparently another customer with a nearly identical last name, picking up a prescription at almost the exact same time.
Somehow our two bags had gotten swapped at the counter.
I called the pharmacy immediately, feeling a little panicked, and they confirmed it right away.
The other customer had actually noticed the same mix-up and had already called about it minutes earlier.
Apparently he'd been just as confused as me, holding a bag of medication he definitely hadn't been prescribed.
He'd been sitting there for a solid ten minutes trying to figure out what had happened.
I drove back that same evening and swapped the bags properly this time.
The pharmacist apologized profusely, double and triple-checking the name on my actual bag, reading it out loud slowly just to be absolutely certain.
Thankfully, neither of us had actually taken anything from the wrong bag.
But it was honestly a little unsettling, realizing how easily that mix-up could have happened with something a lot more serious involved.
The pharmacy manager comped my prescription that visit and apologized again.
He mentioned they were updating their verification process, apparently asking for a birthday now in addition to just a last name, a small change that felt long overdue.

Now, I always double-check the name on the bag myself before leaving the counter, a habit that took one uncomfortable evening to fully develop, but one I definitely don't plan on dropping anytime soon.

I even mentioned the whole story to a friend who works in healthcare, and she said mix-ups like that happen more often than most people realize, which honestly made me want to keep double-checking everything even more carefully from now on.
